case_studies.title: Byte-Exact Deduplication in Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Three-Regime Empirical Analysis Across Public Benchmarks
case_studies.abstract: This preprint presents an empirical analysis of byte-exact chunk-level deduplication in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines. We measure context reduction across three distinct operating regimes: clean academic retrieval (0.16% byte reduction on 22.2M BeIR passages), constructed enterprise patterns (24.03% reduction), and multi-turn conversational AI (80.34% reduction). case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of data duplication in Retrieval-Augmented Generation pipelines by implementing byte-exact deduplication, resulting in significant reductions in data size across various operating regimes. The authors built and tested their approach on different benchmark datasets and APIs. The result shows significant byte reduction, ranging from 0.16% to 80.34%, depending on the regime.

case_studies.title: Iterate Until Retrieved: Factual Nugget Optimization for Discoverable Continual Corrections in Agentic RAG
case_studies.abstract: Agentic retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems in complex B2B (business-to-business) settings may often receive free-form response feedback. Rather than generic feedback signals such as style, preference, or overall response quality, we focus on actionable factual corrections. We identify these instances and convert them into compact knowledge-base entries, which we call factual nuggets. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of handling factual corrections in complex business-to-business settings by building a system called Iterative Nugget Optimization, which creates compact knowledge-base entries called factual nuggets, resulting in improved retrieval-augmented generation systems. The system optimizes these nuggets using the production system as a test harness. This is not directly relevant to cloud infrastructure management

case_studies.title: The Coverage Illusion: From Pre-retrieval Routing Failure to Post-retrieval Cascades in a Production RAG System
case_studies.abstract: In modern RAG pipelines, query augmentation methods such as HyDE and query expansion are applied to every query, resulting in substantial LLM inference costs and increased end-to-end latency. The empirical justification for this overhead in real production traffic remains largely unexplored. We present a case study of the Danish National Encyclopedia, evaluating five retrieval workflows over 20,000 query-workflow pairs from production traffic and synthetic conditions. In this system, synthetic queries suggest that LLM augmentation is needed for over 90% of queries to achieve high retrieval cov
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of inefficient query augmentation methods in RAG pipelines, building a case study to evaluate retrieval workflows and resulting in a finding that LLM augmentation may not be needed for all queries. The study builds on a production RAG system, specifically the Danish National Encyclopedia. The result shows that synthetic queries overestimate the need for LLM augmentation, which could lead to unnecessary costs and latency.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage large language model (LLM) pipelines, here is what to do: review your query augmentation workflows, check for unnecessary LLM inference costs, and consider optimizing your retrieval workflows. This flags a risk: if your org uses automated query expansion or HyDE, check your production traffic to see if you can reduce overhead. Not directly applicable to general IT infrastructure work outside of LLM pipelines.

case_studies.title: In-Context Optimization for Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Gradient-Descent Perspective
case_studies.abstract: In-context learning has recently been linked to implicit gradient descent in linear self-attention models, suggesting that context can induce a forward-pass update. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) also relies on context, but retrieved documents are usually treated as static evidence rather than signals for adaptation. We study RAG as an in-context optimization process. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of optimizing retrieval-augmented generation by treating retrieved documents as signals for adaptation, the authors built a model that implements gradient-descent steps, and the result is a more efficient optimization process. The research focuses on natural language processing and machine learning. It does not directly affect cloud infrastructure management.

case_studies.title: Beyond Semantic Similarity: A Two-Phase Non-Parametric Retrieval Workflow for Corporate Credit Underwriting
case_studies.abstract: Corporate credit underwriting requires analysts to extract actionable evidence from long, heterogeneous financial documents spanning hundreds of pages and multiple languages. Standard Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines optimize for semantic similarity, which frequently surfaces passages that are topically related but lack decision utility, a problem we term the similarity-utility gap. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of retrieving useful information from long financial documents for corporate credit underwriting by building a two-phase non-parametric retrieval workflow, resulting in more relevant and actionable evidence. The workflow separates candidate retrieval from utility ranking, improving decision-making. This is not directly relevant to IT infrastructure work.
